corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the 'crises could be fixed by the Fed / this one is about ideology / different regime' view is the host Niels, continuing his question from C01.
corrections.fix: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen: earlier crises (GFC, pandemic) could be fixed by Fed or fiscal action, but this ideology-driven geopolitical crisis cannot, so it is a different regime that will persist.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: this is Andrew Beer speaking (he continues until 'We'll see.'), not Niels.
corrections.fix: Andrew Beer: either short-term models that exited quickly or broad diversification across many contracts (not concentrated in WTI) may explain which CTAs fared better in March.

corrections.issue: 'Cton down 15%' is most likely Caxton, not Capstone; the list (partly read by Niels) also includes an absolute-return fund down 6.
corrections.fix: Named March 2026 returns: Citadel fixed income about -8%, Brevan Howard -6%, 'Cton' (likely Caxton) -15%, an absolute-return fund -6%, Marshall Wace Eureka -5%, plus wide dispersion among UCITS CTAs.

corrections.issue: Misread: 'shorting the end at 105 or 110 riding it down to 160' refers to shorting the yen (USD/JPY from 105-110 to 160), separate from buying crude oil earlier this year; it is not shorting crude.
corrections.fix: Trend signals pay by catching a few big moves early: shorting Treasuries in Sept 2020 once 10y yields rose from 0.5% to 0.7%, buying gold below 3,000 after a decade of failure, buying crude early this year, and shorting the yen from 105-110 down to 160 per dollar.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: Niels only doubts the numbers; the survivorship/inclusion argument (later, better managers were added to the index) is Andrew Beer's reply.
corrections.fix: Andrew Beer: none of the 2016 index constituents beat the replication; managers that did better were outside that group and were added to the index later, so comparisons against today's index members are biased by inclusion.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader caught all major theses (complexity vs cost, QIS backtest decay, crowding in March) but missed QIS dispersion, wrapper-universe data, several data sources and Niels's counterpoints; 5 speaker/meaning errors.
